texts.preamble: Pradeep Kumar Sah @ Pradeep Sah vs The State Of Bihar on 27 June, 2019 Author: Vikash Jain
texts.facts: 2. The petitioner apprehends his arrest for the offences alleged under Sections 26(2)(i) and 59(iii) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 registered in connection with Memo No. 13/2018 Commissioner of Food Safety Bihar arising out of Excise No. 01/18. 3.
texts.arguments: It is submitted that the petitioner has been falsely implicated and even according to the report of the Food Analyst bearing no. 1183 dated 02.11.2017, the sample merely contained Metanil yellow a non-permitted synthetic colour which is prohibited by law and hence unsafe within the scope of Sec-3(zz)(v) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. However, a decision of this Court in Rajeev Kumar Vs. State of Bihar reported in 2010(3) PLJR 120 is relied upon by the learned counsel to submit that there is nothing in the said report to indicate that yellow synthetic colour was injurious in nature and hence, the petitioner ought not to be prosecuted under the provisions of the said Act.
texts.petitioner_arguments: It is submitted that the petitioner has been falsely implicated and even according to the report of the Food Analyst bearing no. 1183 dated 02.11.2017, the sample merely contained Metanil yellow a non-permitted synthetic colour which is prohibited by law and hence unsafe within the scope of Sec-3(zz)(v) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
